result.title: NOBODY Was There: Bridging the Human-VLM Gap in Unwarranted Person Attribution Bias
result.summary: Describing an image requires not only recognizing what is visible but deciding what should be inferred. We investigate a systematic gap between humans and VLMs in their tendency to attribute visible actions or events to people who are not present in an image. We term this behavior unwarranted person attribution bias and find that, across 25 SOTA VLMs, captions of person-absent scenes mention a person four times as often as human-written captions of the same images. Through a preference study, we further show that both humans and VLMs prefer captions that avoid such attributions. Motivated by this, we introduce NOBODY, a preference dataset designed to bridge the gap between humans and VLMs in unwarranted person attribution. Through direct preference optimization (DPO), we align open VLMs on NOBODY and show that their agreement with human captions on person attribution reaches or exceeds inter-human agreement, whereas nine existing public preference datasets leave this behavior largely unchanged. Furthermore, we show that human judges preferred the aligned VLM captions significantly more than those of the baseline model. Alongside NOBODY, we release NOBODY-Bench, which evaluates VLMs for unwarranted person attribution bias and their alignment against human captions and preference. Project page: https://pmadinei.github.io/NOBODY/

AI.brief_summary: 论文定义并量化了 VLM 的「无据人物归因偏差」：在 25 个 SOTA 模型上，无人场景的生成描述提及人物的频率约为人类书写描述的 4 倍，且人与模型都更偏好避免此类归因的描述；作者据此构建偏好数据集 NOBODY 与评测基准 NOBODY-Bench，并用 DPO 对齐后使模型的人物归因与人类一致度接近或超过人际一致度。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接诊断了生成内容超出可见视觉证据的失败模式，与「视觉细节是否被保留和正确使用」「视觉证据筛选」这一关切相关，可供核查生成侧的幻觉度量与偏好监督能否用于判断 latent 推理是否真正依据图像；但材料未涉及 latent 状态、推理轨迹或动态计算。
